query: How is the price of anarchy defined and measured in game theory?
ground_truth_answer: The price of anarchy is defined by comparing the ratio of the social welfare of the centralized solution to that of the social welfare of the Nash equilibrium with the worst social welfare (assuming a positive social welfare function). It quantifies the cost of using a decentralized solution compared to an optimal centralized one.

query: Why does replacing an exact VCG mechanism with an approximation create issues according to Nisan and Ronen?
ground_truth_answer: Replacing a VCG mechanism by an approximation does not preserve truthfulness. Even though truthfully revealing one's private type is an optimal strategy in an exact VCG mechanism, it may no longer be optimal in an approximation.

query: What is the computational complexity of the winner determination problem in combinatorial auctions?
ground_truth_answer: The winner determination problem is NP-complete in general, even in relatively simple classes of combinatorial auctions with only two bidders making rather restricted bids, and it is not polynomial-time approximable.

query: In traffic routing, what is the maximum price of anarchy when travel time is a linear function of congestion?
expected_text_match: price of anarchy is at most 4/3
ground_truth_answer: Roughgarden and Tardos showed that if travel time is a linear function of congestion, the price of anarchy is at most 4/3.

query: Under what condition regarding the number of faulty nodes t and total nodes n can Byzantine agreement be reached?
expected_text_match: fewer than a third of the agents
ground_truth_answer: In the presence of Byzantine failures, agreement can be reached if and only if fewer than a third of the agents can be faulty (t < n/3).

query: Is deterministic consensus possible in an asynchronous system with crash failures?
ground_truth_answer: No, in an asynchronous system, it is impossible to reach agreement using a deterministic protocol even if there is at most one failure (t = 1) and only crash failures are allowed.

query: What is the computational complexity class of finding a Nash equilibrium in normal-form games?
ground_truth_answer: Finding a Nash equilibrium in normal-form games is a PPAD-complete (polynomial parity argument, directed case) problem.

query: What does the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem state regarding strategic voting in nondictatorial voting schemes?
ground_truth_answer: The Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem shows that if there are at least three alternatives, then in any nondictatorial voting scheme, there exist preferences under which an agent is better off voting strategically rather than ranking candidates by their true preferences.

query: What file sharing patterns were observed in empirical studies of the Gnutella P2P network?
ground_truth_answer: Studies of the Gnutella network by Adar and Huberman showed that almost 70 percent of users share no files, and nearly 50 percent of all responses originate from the top 1 percent of sharing hosts.

query: What can be achieved when implementing mediators using cheap talk if n > 3k + 3t holds?
expected_text_match: requires no knowledge of other agents
ground_truth_answer: If n > 3k + 3t, a (k, t)-robust strategy with a mediator can be implemented using cheap talk. This implementation requires no knowledge of other agents' utilities, and the cheap talk protocol has a bounded running time that does not depend on utilities.

query: What are the parametric and non-parametric memory components of RAG models?
ground_truth_answer: In RAG models, the parametric memory is a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence transformer (BART-large), and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed using a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR).

query: How do RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token differ in their use of retrieved passages during text generation?
ground_truth_answer: RAG-Sequence conditions on the same retrieved document across the entire generated sequence, whereas RAG-Token can use and marginalize over different retrieved passages for each individual generated token.

query: Why is the document encoder kept fixed during RAG model fine-tuning?
expected_text_match: costly as it requires the document index
ground_truth_answer: The document encoder (BERTd) is kept fixed because updating it during training is computationally costly, requiring periodic re-indexing of the entire document collection. Only the query encoder (BERTq) and BART generator are fine-tuned.

query: How is the Wikipedia knowledge source chunked and indexed in the RAG experiments?
ground_truth_answer: Using the December 2018 Wikipedia dump, each Wikipedia article is split into disjoint 100-word chunks, yielding a total of 21 million documents. Embeddings are computed with the document encoder and indexed using FAISS with HNSW approximation.

query: What advantage does generative answer formulation offer over extractive QA approaches in open-domain QA?
ground_truth_answer: Documents containing clues about the answer without containing the answer verbatim can still contribute towards generating a correct answer, which is not possible with standard extractive reader architectures.

query: What were the results of human evaluations regarding factuality when comparing BART and RAG on Jeopardy question generation?
expected_text_match: more factual than RAG in only 7.1%
ground_truth_answer: In human evaluations across 452 generation pairs, BART was found to be more factual than RAG in only 7.1% of cases, whereas RAG was more factual in 42.7% of cases (with both deemed good in an additional 17% of cases).

query: What is the total number of trainable parameters in the fine-tuned RAG models?
ground_truth_answer: RAG models have a total of 626M trainable parameters: 110M from the DPR BERT-base query encoder and 406M from the BART-large sequence-to-sequence generator (the document encoder is not trained).

query: What was demonstrated by the index hot-swapping experiment using 2016 and 2018 Wikipedia dumps?
ground_truth_answer: The experiment demonstrated that RAG's world knowledge can be updated dynamically at test time without any retraining simply by replacing the non-parametric index: RAG answered 70% correctly for 2016 world leaders using the 2016 index and 68% for 2018 world leaders using the 2018 index.

query: How does the Thorough Decoding procedure operate for RAG-Sequence models?
expected_text_match: additional forward pass for each document
ground_truth_answer: In Thorough Decoding, beam search is run for each retrieved document. To estimate the marginal probability of a candidate hypothesis y, an additional forward pass is run for every document where y did not appear in the beam, multiplying generator probabilities by retriever probabilities and summing across all beams.

query: What is retrieval collapse and how does it manifest during training?
expected_text_match: learn to retrieve the same documents
ground_truth_answer: Retrieval collapse occurs when the retrieval component learns to retrieve the same set of documents regardless of the input, causing the generator to ignore retrieved documents and behave essentially identically to a parametric-only baseline like BART.

conversation_history.content: What is a combinatorial auction and why is communicating bids challenging in such auctions?

A combinatorial auction allows bidders to bid on bundles of items. Communicating bids is challenging because with n items there are 2^n possible bundles, which can require exponential communication length in general.

query: What is the computational complexity of solving its winner determination problem?
ground_truth_answer: The winner determination problem in combinatorial auctions is NP-complete in general (even with only two bidders making restricted bids) and is not polynomial-time approximable.

conversation_history.content: What is the Byzantine agreement problem in distributed computing?

The Byzantine agreement problem involves n soldiers/agents, up to t of which may be faulty, where nonfaulty agents must reach the exact same decision (such as attack or retreat), matching their initial preferences if all nonfaulty agents agree.

query: Under what condition can it be solved if faulty agents exhibit malicious behavior?
ground_truth_answer: In the presence of Byzantine (malicious) failures, agreement can be reached if and only if fewer than a third of the agents are faulty (t < n/3).

conversation_history.content: How is the price of anarchy applied to traffic routing problems?

In traffic routing, travel time increases with congestion. The price of anarchy measures the cost of using decentralized selfish routing compared to an optimal centralized assignment that minimizes total average travel time.

query: How does this metric behave when the travel latency function is nonlinear versus linear?
ground_truth_answer: The price of anarchy is unbounded if the travel time is a nonlinear function of congestion, but is at most 4/3 if the travel time is a linear function.

conversation_history.content: What are the two formulations of RAG models: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token?
RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the entire output sequence, whereas RAG-Token can retrieve and marginalize over different documents across each generated token.

query: How does the decoding procedure work for the first model during test time?
expected_text_match: run beam search for each document
ground_truth_answer: For RAG-Sequence, beam search is run per retrieved document to obtain candidate hypotheses Y. In Thorough Decoding, additional forward passes score hypotheses across documents where they did not appear in the beam before summing marginal probabilities; Fast Decoding approximates ungenerated hypotheses as zero probability to avoid extra passes.

conversation_history.content: What is index hot-swapping in non-parametric memory models like RAG?

Index hot-swapping is the ability to update the model's factual knowledge dynamically at test time without any model retraining, simply by replacing the underlying non-parametric document index with a newer version.

query: How was this capability validated using world leader queries from different years?
ground_truth_answer: Index hot-swapping was validated using 82 world leaders that changed between 2016 and 2018: RAG achieved 70% accuracy for 2016 leaders with the 2016 index and 68% for 2018 leaders with the 2018 index, while mismatched index-query pairs dropped significantly (to 4%-12%).

conversation_history.content: How do RAG models perform on the Jeopardy question generation task?
On Jeopardy question generation, RAG models outperform BART baselines in Q-BLEU-1, and human evaluators rated RAG generations as significantly more factual (42.7% vs 7.1%) and specific.

query: Why does it perform particularly well on these questions that combine multiple pieces of information?
ground_truth_answer: RAG-Token performs well on multi-fact questions because it can draw and combine information from several retrieved documents for different tokens within the same generated output, while leveraging parametric memory to complete known entity names.
